title: Turkey Oak: Ancient Turkey Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: A fast, tall Balkan oak planted on purpose: Genoa's reaches 41 metres, taller than the redwood beside it; Utrecht counts four as one register entry.
intro: Quercus cerris is an oak of southern and southeastern Europe and Asia Minor, and north of its range every one was planted on purpose: gardeners liked how fast it grows and how large it gets while the person who planted it is still around to see it. Genoa's, in the English-style grounds of Villa Serra above the city, is the surprise: 41 metres, taller than the Californian redwood sixty metres away. Caserta's grows in the royal park's English Garden among trees collected from Australia and California, while the species grows wild in the hills a few kilometres away. Utrecht's four stand together on an old city-wall bastion, close enough that the Dutch register counts them as one entry. The leaves give it away: stiffer and more deeply cut than a pedunculate oak's, with whiskery bud scales and mossy, curl-wrapped acorn cups.
